manifest.name: dsh-plugin-wsl-env
manifest.description: 在 WSL 的 Linux 实例中打开项目工作区，在对应 Linux 空间中进行命令执行、运行 shell 脚本和文件访问，以获得全套 Linux Shell 工具链收益，并通过 bubblewrap 对命令进行沙箱隔离

scripts.test: pnpm run lint:style && pnpm run lint:links && pnpm run lint:requirements && pnpm run test:syntax && pnpm run lint:build && pnpm run lint:types && pnpm run test:unit
scripts.test:unit: node scripts/test-watchdog.mjs -- node --test --test-timeout=60000 test/fs.boot.test.mjs test/fsio-text.test.mjs test/composition.test.mjs test/provider.test.mjs test/file-reference-wsl.test.mjs test/paths.test.mjs test/listing.test.mjs ...

bundle.text:
# The bundle layer this package contributes:
#
#     "dsh": { "bundle": { "patch": "./cordis.patch.yml" } }
#
# `dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-plugin-wsl-env` installs the package and
# appends this file as one layer — there is nothing to merge by hand. It is
# still an ordinary patch layer: a top-level YAML array of loader patch entries
# (id-targeted config overrides, disables, and insert lists; `!!js` expressions
# allowed).
#
# Layers compose in the order bundles, the profile's own `cordis.patch.yml`,
# the home-level `cordis.patch.yml`, then `--patch` overlays, and later layers
# win per row. A row's `config` is replaced whole, never deep-merged, so a user
# who wants a different value overrides that row by id in their own layer —
# examples/profile.cordis.patch.yml shows what such a layer looks like.
#
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# The GUI terminal window is a COMPOSITION-level environment, not a preset one.
#
# The right-sidebar terminal is dsh-api-terminal-controller. It resolves its
# execution world from the Session's own context —
#     agent.ctx.get("subprocess")
# — and that context is created by the agent loop under the ROOT realm
# (dsh-agent-loop: `createScope(loopCtx, …)`, loopCtx = the root `ctx.agents`),
# while a preset's isolate realms are created by dsh-agent-preset-registry under
# the REGISTRY's context (`createScope(this.owner, …)`). The two subtrees never
# meet, so a `subprocess` provider mounted inside preset-wsl — the natural-looking
# design, since `shell` and `fs` live there — is invisible to the terminal
# window. The registry ships `agentPresets.serviceFor(agent, name)` for exactly
# that gap; the terminal controller does not use it.
#
# So the terminal is bound here, once, for the whole composition:
#
#   1. the shipped local provider is disabled and replaced by a subclass whose
#      ONLY override is `spawnTerminal`, which rewrites a `wsl.exe` launch into
#      `wsl.exe -d <distro> --cd <linux dir>` for the directory the Session
#      supplies. Ordinary `spawn()` — every command, the host ripgrep search,
#      every other consumer — reaches the shipped implementation untouched;
#   2. the controller is given the composition's default shell profile (the
#      distro shell, so a directory-less launch lands in the distro rather than
#      `cmd.exe` inside a UNC workspace) plus host candidates. The default must
#      stay static — the controller resolves it without a Session — but the
#      candidates make the shell menu honest: `wsl.exe` dedupes into the
#      default's `wsl` kind, and `powershell`/`cmd` are launches this terminal
#      really starts (host sessions run PowerShell outright, and a manually
#      selected shell is titled after itself — the sanctioned bridge over the
#      fixed tab title, see docs/UPSTREAM-TERMINAL-TITLE.md).
#
# Consequence: a terminal's EXECUTION WORLD follows the Session — a WSL-folder
# session runs the distro's shell, a Windows-folder session runs PowerShell in
# its own directory (`hostSessions` on `subprocess-wsl`) — while the DEFAULT
# entry and its title stay the composition's single `WSL` profile, which no
# Session identity reaches. The title that implies is documented in
# docs/LIMITATIONS.md and bridged upstream in docs/UPSTREAM-TERMINAL-TITLE.md.
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
- id: subprocess
  disabled: true

- id: terminal-controller
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-terminal-controller'
  config:
    shell:
      path: wsl.exe
      name: WSL
      args: []
    shellCandidates:
      - wsl.exe
      - powershell
      - cmd

- insert:
    - id: subprocess-wsl
      name: 'dsh-plugin-wsl-env/subprocess'
      config:
        # auto: follow the launch directory's UNC distro; "default" forces WSL's
        # default, and a name pins. Empty is auto.
        distro: ''

# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Environment is per-session, not per-process.
#
# There is no DSH_WSL switch any more. The profile keeps the SHIPPED environment
# for host workspaces — sandboxed PowerShell executor, ACL-confined filesystem,
# and therefore the Permissions selector — while the wsl agent preset (appended
# below) supplies the WSL environment to agents that select it, isolated to that
# preset's own service realm. Both can run at the same time in one process.
#
# dsh-plugin-wsl-env/auto-preset binds the WSL preset automatically when a new
# session's workspace directory is inside a distro, and leaves an explicit
# operator choice alone.
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ── The workspace picker serves BOTH worlds ──────────────────────────────────
#
# Kept from the previous design: the shipped chooser resolves to the native OS
# dialog on Windows, which cannot browse a distro. This one lists the Windows home
# directory and every installed distro in its root level, so it is the single
# picker for host and WSL workspaces alike — and the directory it returns is what
# auto-preset reads to choose the environment.
- id: directory-picker
  disabled: true

- insert:
    - id: directory-picker-wsl
      name: 'dsh-plugin-wsl-env/picker'
      config:
        preferredDistro: ''
        includeHostHome: true
        maxEntries: 1000

    - id: directory-picker-browse-surface
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-directory-picker-browse'

# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# The distro-side takeover of the root-plane filesystem.
#
# A patch layer is a flat list: an `id:` entry patches the shipped row, and a
# bare `insert:` list appends new rows as data. A disable written INSIDE an
# insert list is not a patch — it becomes a duplicate-id data row that shadows
# the real service row (the loader keys rows by id, last occurrence wins), and
# a nested `insert:` list is never interpreted at all. This takeover is
# therefore two top-level entries: disable the shipped row by id, then append
# the replacement with a bare insert. test/composition.test.mjs runs this file
# through the real patch algorithm to keep the shape honest.
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# The GUI file service keeps the shipped `workspace-files` row: its client half
# is the browser `file` resource provider the Sidebar previews need, and a
# server-only replacement drops it (docs/LIMITATIONS.md). The shipped service
# reads WSL paths through the routed root filesystem below, so the GUI file tree
# and previews still run inside the distro, at the cost of a few extra agent
# round trips.

# The root-plane filesystem routes by coordinate: distro UNC identities are
# served by the resident agent (real watch events, ext4 reads), drive paths
# stay host-native. Replaces the root fs-sandbox row, whose write fence has no
# root-plane consumers (the model's writes ride the preset filesystems; see
# docs/root-fs-routing.md).
- id: fs-sandbox
  disabled: true

- insert:
    - id: fs-routing
      name: 'dsh-plugin-wsl-env/fs-routing'
      config:
        # auto: route each UNC target to its own distro; "default" forces WSL's
        # default, and a name pins. Empty is auto.
        distro: ''
        wslPath: wsl.exe
        sandbox: true
        maskWindowsDrive: false
        restrictToDistro: true
        watchMaxDepth: 0
    # Contributes the WSL environment's facts (distro / real shell / home) to the
    # managed DSH_* namespace that dsh-shell-env injects into every model shell
    # call. That is DSH's sanctioned channel for shell-environment facts.
    - id: wsl-shell-env
      name: 'dsh-plugin-wsl-env/shell-env'

    # Per-session environment selection from the workspace directory. It only
    # rewrites a preset that still equals the registry default, so an operator's
    # explicit choice is never overridden.
    - id: auto-preset
      name: 'dsh-plugin-wsl-env/auto-preset'

    # Session-start sandbox preflight: when a distro session opens, run the
    # providers' own bwrap usability probe (shared cache, so the first confined
    # command pays nothing) and surface a missing or broken bubblewrap as a
    # warning with the full remedy — instead of the first command's fail-closed
    # error being the discovery moment. Advisory only: it never installs and
    # never changes the providers' fail-closed semantics.
    - id: wsl-preflight
      name: 'dsh-plugin-wsl-env/preflight'

- insert:
    # ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # preset-wsl — the WSL environment, scoped to agents that select this preset.
    #
    # This is what makes environments per-session instead of per-process: the shell
    # and fs services are isolated to this preset's realm, so an agent on the host
    # preset keeps the profile's global sandboxed PowerShell executor and ACL-confined
    # filesystem while an agent on this preset gets the distro's login shell and its
    # UNC-backed filesystem — concurrently, in one process.
    #
    # The wrapping group is required by dsh-agent-preset-registry, which audits every
    # preset mount and rejects a provider that is not behind an isolate realm:
    #     "Preset services require isolate realms: shell, fs"
    # Because a preset's plugins mount under a REGISTRY-owned scope (not this row's
    # ctx), the realm has to be declared here, inside config.plugins.
    #
    # Generated from the shipped standard preset so the embedded plan-mode
    # section and every nested group survive byte-for-byte: this copy is
    # `packages/bundle/web-app/presets/standard.patch.yml` of the
    # `dsh-v0.2.2-rc.1` source tree, changed
    # in exactly three ways —
    #   1. every shipped row mounts inside `wsl-env`, so the preset's tools see
    #      the distro's shell and fs (the realm is declared on the group);
    #   2. `tool-bash` is enabled and `tool-pwsh` disabled outright, where the
    #      shipped copy derives the choice from `process.platform`;
    #   3. the identity and display metadata: row `preset-wsl`, preset `wsl`,
    #      `name`/`description` for the mode selector, `order: 2`.
    # Regenerate it when an app update changes the preset: take
    # `packages/bundle/web-app/presets/standard.patch.yml` from the harness tree
    # the peer pins track and run `node scripts/build-preset-wsl.mjs <that
    # file>`, then replace this row to the end of the file. The script applies
    # changes 1 and 2 itself, so only change 3 is yours.
    # ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    - id: preset-wsl
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset'
      config:
        id: wsl
        # Display metadata: `wsl` is not a registry built-in id, so the mode
        # selector falls back to the raw id and "no description" unless the
        # declaration carries its own copy (registry policy: user-authored
        # metadata is never localized — write it in the deployment language).
        name: WSL 模式
        description: 在 WSL 的 Linux 实例中打开项目工作区：命令执行、shell 脚本和文件访问均在 Linux 空间内完成，以获得全套 Linux shell 工具链，受限命令经 bubblewrap 沙箱隔离。
        order: 2
        plugins:
          - id: wsl-env
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              shell: true
              fs: true
            config:
              # ── the WSL environment for this preset only ────────────────────
              # No `cwd`: an empty default workdir means the distro user's home,
              # asked of the distro itself. Pin a directory here to override it —
              # a value that is right on one machine is wrong on every other.
              #
              # Commands run in one persistent systemd user scope per session
              # (ADR 0001): a background dev server survives the command that
              # started it, `/tmp` is the distro's real `/tmp`, and `ps` sees the
              # session. This needs systemd as PID 1 (`[boot] systemd=true` in
              # /etc/wsl.conf) and a lingering user manager (`loginctl
              # enable-linger <user>`); the preflight refuses with those remedies
              # when one is missing. Set `sessionSandbox: false` for the old
              # per-command shape. Bubblewrap is still required for the mount
              # profile; without it the providers fail closed.
              - id: wsl-shell
                name: 'dsh-plugin-wsl-env'
                config:
                  # auto: follow the request workdir's UNC distro; "default"
                  # forces WSL's default, and a name pins. Empty is auto.
                  distro: ''
                  loginShell: true
                  timeoutMs: 120000
                  maxTimeoutMs: 600000
                  sessionSandbox: true
                  # auto: the native session-runtime agent when a verified
                  # source is available (packaged binary, or the
                  # DSH_WSL_AGENT_NATIVE development override); otherwise the
                  # shipped shell agent. native fails the first command instead
                  # of falling back; shell forces the shell agent.
                  agentBackend: auto
              - id: wsl-fs
                name: 'dsh-plugin-wsl-env/fs'
                config:
                  # auto: follow each target path's UNC distro; "default"
                  # forces WSL's default, and a name pins. Empty is auto.
                  distro: ''
                  restrictToDistro: true
                  # agent (the default): reads/writes/identities run inside the
                  # distro over the resident agent (lib/fs-substrate.js) —
                  # native symlinks and mode bits, the write guard survives to
                  # publication, and confined mutations are kernel-enforced.
                  # "share" is retired; a profile carrying it is refused at boot.
                  substrate: agent
                  # Confined writes ride the session runtime (ADR 0001), so they
                  # share the command's real /tmp and workspace mounts.
                  sessionSandbox: true
              - id: persona
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona'
                config:
                  prefix: You are a coding agent powered by the {{model}} model.
              - id: agent-instructions
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions'
                config:
                  maxBytes: 65536
              - id: time-context
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-time-context'
              - id: tool-bash
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash'
                disabled: false
              - id: tool-pwsh
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-pwsh'
                disabled: true
              - id: tool-fs
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs'
                config:
                  # Set false to drop the apply_patch tool beside edit. The
                  # base patchText is the host-side implementation; the distro
                  # substrate serves read/write/edit itself and must not have
                  # a patch path that quietly crosses the 9p share instead.
                  applyPatch: false
              - id: tool-fs-search
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs-search'
                config:
                  sampleOverCapGlobResults: false
              - id: tool-jobs
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-jobs'
              - id: tool-schedule
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-schedule'
              - id: skill-filesystem
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem'
              - id: tool-skill
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill'
              - id: command-goal
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-goal'
              - id: tool-goal
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-goal'
              - id: planning
                name: cordis:group
                group: true
                isolate:
                  planMode: true
                config:
                  - id: plan-mode
                    name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plan-mode'
                    config:
                      section: |
                        You are in plan mode. Stay in plan mode until the user approves your plan through exit_plan_mode or switches the session mode. Imperative language to implement changes means plan the implementation, not execute it. A user's conversational agreement — including an answer confirming something you asked — approves nothing and does not end plan mode; fold the confirmed decision into the plan and submit it through exit_plan_mode.

                        Explore first. Use non-mutating reads, searches, static analysis, and checks to ground the plan in the actual repository. Do not edit or write files, change configuration, run formatters or code generation that rewrites tracked files, commit, or otherwise carry out the plan. Prefer existing functions and patterns over new machinery.

                        The tool catalog stays the same across modes for request-cache stability. These plan-mode rules override any later tool description or guidance that suggests using mutation tools; those tools remain listed to keep the tool catalog unchanged. Do not use todo_write to track this planning phase: it tracks implementation after an approved plan, while the plan itself belongs in exit_plan_mode.

                        Resolve discoverable facts by inspection. Use ask_user_question only for user-owned choices or material ambiguity that inspection cannot answer. Do not ask the user where code lives or how current behavior works when you can find out.

                        Make the plan decision-complete: state the goal and success criteria; group implementation changes by subsystem; identify public API, schema, and data-flow changes; cover edge cases, failure modes, tests, acceptance criteria, and explicit assumptions. Keep it concise enough to review but detailed enough that another engineer can implement it without making design decisions.

                        When ready, call exit_plan_mode with the complete plan markdown, starting with a # title. Make exit_plan_mode the only and final tool call in that assistant response: it presents the plan for approval, and implementation begins only in a later step after approval. Do not paste the final plan as a plain reply or ask "should I proceed?" through prose or ask_user_question. If review rejects it, incorporate the feedback and present again. If the review channel is unavailable or aborted, stay in plan mode and ask the user to switch modes manually; do not proceed with implementation.
              - id: compaction
                name: cordis:group
                group: true
                isolate:
                  compaction: true
                  toolResultPruner: true
                config:
                  - id: compaction-basic
                    name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic'
                  - id: command-compact
                    name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-compact'
                  - id: tool-result-pruner
                    name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-tool-result-pruner'
                    config:
                      thresholdChars: 8192
                      headChars: 4096
                      tailChars: 1024
              - id: delegation
                name: cordis:group
                group: true
                isolate:
                  workflowEngine: true
                config:
                  - id: tool-subagent-control
                    name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control'
                  - id: tool-subagent
                    name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                    config:
                      provider: spawn
                      toolName: subagent
                      modelSelection: true
                      modelDiscovery: true
                  - id: tool-subagent-fork
                    name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                    config:
                      provider: fork
                      toolName: subagent_fork
                  - id: workflow-ptc
                    name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-ptc'
                    config:
                      provider: spawn
                  - id: tool-workflow
                    name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-workflow'
              - id: tool-ask-user
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ask-user'
              - id: tool-todo
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-todo'
                config:
                  allowParallelInProgress: true
              - id: tool-web
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-web'
                config:
                  fetch: true
                  searchTimeoutMs: 60000
              - id: present
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-present'
              - id: tool-plugin-manager
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-manager/tools'
                disabled: !!js "!ctx.get('profileContext')"
              - id: tool-plugin-market
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-market/tools'
                disabled: true

readme.text:
**English** · [中文](docs/README.zh.md)

[](https://github.com/Big-Dao/dsh-plugin-wsl-env/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-wsl-env)
[](LICENSE)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that opens the project workspace inside a WSL 2 distribution on Windows.

The harness process stays on Windows. Command execution, shell scripts and file access all run in the distro's Linux environment for the full Linux shell toolchain. No helper service or daemon is installed, no port is opened, and confined commands run under `bubblewrap`.

Windows + WSL 2 only.

**New here?** Start with [docs/QUICKSTART.md](docs/QUICKSTART.md) — prerequisites, recipes and the compatibility table.

If the harness itself can run in the distro, it is simpler **not** to use this
plugin: install the CLI there and run it from the distro's shell. No UNC paths,
no 9p round trips, no Windows-to-distro agent.

```bash

readme.section: inside the distro; the CLI needs Node >= 24.9
readme.text:
npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh
dsh web                       # browser UI, reached through WSL's localhost forwarding
dsh headless "run the tests"  # one task, one answer, exit
```

Use this plugin when the harness has to stay on Windows:

readme.section: inside the distro; the CLI needs Node >= 24.9
readme.text:
| Your setup | What to use |
|---|---|
| Work happens inside WSL; a terminal or browser UI is enough | the CLI installed in the distro |
| You want the Windows desktop app, with commands and files in the distro | this plugin |
| One session must reach Windows and WSL folders at once | this plugin — per-path routing is the point |

readme.section: inside the distro; the CLI needs Node >= 24.9
readme.text:
Mixing the two has one trap: the `desktop` profile name is owned by the Electron
app, and the npm CLI refuses to manage that profile's plugins — use the app's
Plugins page for it. [docs/VALUE.zh.md](docs/VALUE.zh.md) has the full
comparison and the cases this plugin is not for.

A Windows coding tool that works on WSL projects has three options: run the whole tool inside the distro, connect to a helper server inside the distro, or let the plugin provide the distro environment. This plugin is the third option. One workflow covers both kinds of session, with the distro's real tools and the command sandbox intact.

- **Real Linux environment.** Commands run in the distro's own login shell. Its `PATH`, `nvm`, `cargo`, `pyenv` and rc files apply. File tools access distro paths through an in-distro agent; the backing filesystem depends on the path.
- **No service in the distro.** There is no helper server, no daemon and no listening port. The only persisted artifact is a content-addressed copy of the native agent in `~/.cache/dsh-wsl/agent/`.
- **Sandboxed by default.** Confined commands run under `bubblewrap` inside the distro. If `bubblewrap` is missing, the command fails; it does not run unconfined.
- **Per-session.** A session opened on a distro folder gets the distro environment. A session opened on a Windows folder keeps the normal Windows tools. Both can run in one harness process.
- **Integrated with the GUI.** The folder picker lists installed distros, the terminal opens a shell in the distro, and the model can see listening ports.

Most coding agents learn from Linux-first material, and most open-source toolchains are built and tested on Linux first. Asking an agent to work through a Windows shell adds a translation layer on every call:

- **Training prior.** Examples, CI scripts, Dockerfiles and most public answers use POSIX shells and GNU tools. A model's first instinct is `bash`, not PowerShell.
- **Toolchain support.** Node, Python, Rust, Go, C/C++ and most build systems are validated on Linux first. Windows support is often a port with different quoting, paths, line endings and file locking.
- **Shell semantics.** PowerShell and `cmd` differ from POSIX in quoting, escaping, pipelines, environment variables, exit codes and path separators. Mixing the two produces errors that look like model mistakes.
- **Environment drift.** Windows setups vary by PowerShell version, execution policy, PATH and installed tools. Linux environments are easier to reproduce and containerize.

The result is more failed commands, more retries and more time spent on syntax instead of the task. Generated code is affected too: shell snippets, build commands and CI-style one-liners are usually written for POSIX, and the distro is where they run unchanged. A real Linux login shell removes that translation layer. Modern PowerShell and Windows-native toolchains narrow the gap, but the default prior and most project scripts still assume POSIX.
This plugin keeps the GUI on Windows and moves only the execution environment into the distro, so the agent gets the shell that its training and the toolchain both assume.

| | Desktop remote (VS Code, ZCode) | This plugin |
|---|---|---|
| Inside the distro | a helper server | one cached agent binary |
| Network | a listening port | none |
| Command sandbox | none | `bubblewrap` |
| Removal | delete the server | delete the cache |

A desktop remote reconnects faster and is more mature. A CLI agent installed inside WSL is simpler if it covers your work. This plugin is for the case where the harness stays on Windows and commands must be sandboxed.

- Windows 10 or 11 with WSL 2 and at least one distro.
- `bubblewrap` in the distro. It is required.
- systemd in the distro for the default session sandbox: set `[boot] systemd=true` in `/etc/wsl.conf`, restart WSL, then run `loginctl enable-linger "$USER"` once. Without systemd, set `sessionSandbox: false` on both `wsl-shell` and `wsl-fs`.
- Optional: `ripgrep` for search, `git` for change snapshots, `inotify-tools` for file watching.

No Node.js is required inside the distro.

The Windows desktop app ships **no `dsh` executable**: the installer writes
`DeepSeek Harness.exe`, and the CLI entry lives inside `resources/app.asar`
(the probe scripts launch it through `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`). Use the
distribution you have.

**Desktop app.** Open **Plugins** in the sidebar, choose **Add plugin**, enter
the exact package name `dsh-plugin-wsl-env`, then enable it. The plugin manager
writes the active profile's `package.json` — the dependency and the
`dsh.profile.bundles` entry — which is the same state the CLI command below
produces. To run from a checkout, add it as a linked package instead of a
name. Start it the way the installer's shortcut does: `DeepSeek Harness.exe`,
no arguments. The app opens the profile it is configured with — the one the
Plugins page writes into — so a different profile is a CLI-distribution thing
(`dsh --profile <name>`).

**CLI distribution** (`dsh` on `PATH`), in a Windows terminal:

```powershell
dsh wsl --from-default-profile web --dump-config   # create a profile named wsl
dsh plugin --profile wsl add dsh-plugin-wsl-env    # install the plugin and its settings
dsh --profile wsl --dump-config                    # verify: prints "# == dsh-plugin-wsl-env"
dsh --profile wsl                                  # start

Install `bubblewrap` before the first command:

From a checkout, `pnpm run doctor` is the one-command environment check: Windows/WSL versions, the distro and its shell, bubblewrap usability, systemd / the user manager / Linger, the optional tools, peer versions, the agent cache, a fresh-agent handshake, stale session scopes and the known profile-patch trap. Each failure prints one copy-paste remedy; `--json` is for scripts, and `--fix` sweeps stale scopes (package installation needs `--fix --install` and an explicit confirmation). `pnpm run diagnose` is its read-only alias. `pnpm run bootstrap <distro>` remains the narrower tool-install helper.

Upgrade by installing again (Plugins page, or the `add` command). Uninstall on
the Plugins page, or with `dsh plugin --profile wsl remove dsh-plugin-wsl-env`
where the CLI is installed; the agent cache under `~/.cache/dsh-wsl` can then be
deleted. If you added a local `workspace-files-wsl` workaround to your profile to
restore previews, remove it after upgrading: the plugin no longer mounts that
row.
Open a distro folder as the workspace, for example `\\wsl.localhost\ubuntu\home\you\project`.

- Opening a folder in any distro runs there, even when it is not WSL's default.
- Commands run in the distro's login shell. `/home/you/x` and `\\wsl.localhost\ubuntu\home\you\x` are the same file.
- **New terminal** opens a shell in the same distro and directory.
- The model sees listening ports and can return the URL of a dev server. WSL 2 forwards localhost to Windows.
- The Permissions selector offers `read-only`, `workspace-write` (default) and `danger-full-access`. Only `danger-full-access` runs without the sandbox.
Settings live on named rows in `$DSH_HOME/profiles/<name>/cordis.patch.yml`. The main values:

| Row | Key | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wsl-shell` | `distro` | `''` | distro mode; empty/`auto` follows the workspace, `default` forces WSL's default |
| | `sandbox` | `true` | confine commands with `bubblewrap` |
| | `sessionSandbox` | shipped `true` | run the session's commands in one systemd user scope |
| | `agentBackend` | `auto` | `auto`, `native` or `shell` for the in-distro agent |
| | `maskWindowsDrive` | `false` | hide `/mnt` from confined commands |
| `wsl-fs` | `distro` | `''` | distro mode; empty/`auto` follows each target path |
| | `restrictToDistro` | `true` | under a fixed distro, refuse paths that belong to another distro |
| | `sandbox` | `true` | check confined writes against the policy |
| | `sessionSandbox` | shipped `true` | run confined writes in the session runtime |
| | `substrate` | `agent` | in-distro agent; `share` is rejected at startup |
| `directory-picker-wsl` | `includeHostHome` | `true` | also list the Windows home directory |
| `subprocess-wsl` | `distro` | `''` | distro mode; empty/`auto` follows the launch directory |

`fs-routing` is the top-level router for root-level `ctx.fs` calls: its distro
settings are independent of `wsl-fs`, and it is a top-level row patched by id
like the others. `wsl-shell` and `wsl-fs` are inside the shipped `wsl` preset,
so overriding them by id does not work. Override the whole `preset-wsl` row
instead; [docs/CONFIGURATION.md](docs/CONFIGURATION.md) has the recipe and the
remaining keys. [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml) is the commented
reference for every shipped value.

One harness process can serve Windows-folder and distro-folder sessions at the same time. Services attach at two levels:

```text
app level (one per process)
├─ directory-picker-wsl, workspace-files, subprocess-wsl
├─ fs-routing: root filesystem routed by path
└─ auto-preset: binds the wsl preset when a session opens a distro folder

- `wsl-shell` runs commands through one resident agent inside a systemd user scope. The agent is the packaged static-musl `dsh-wsl-agent` for the distro's architecture (`x86_64` or `aarch64`), with the shell agent as fallback. Each command runs in the login shell under a `bubblewrap` mount profile. The scope outlives the command, so background servers survive and `ps` sees the session. With `sessionSandbox: false`, the agent stays per distro and each command gets its own profile.
- `wsl-fs` serves reads and writes through the same in-distro agent. Confined writes run in a long-lived agent whose mount profile matches the policy, so the kernel enforces the write boundary. There is no host-side file fallback: if the agent is unavailable, file operations fail.
- The GUI file tree and previews are the shipped `workspace-files` row, not a plugin replacement: its client half is the browser `file` provider. It reads WSL paths through the routed root filesystem, so it stays distro-side, at the cost of a few extra agent round trips.
- App-level services route by path. A distro UNC path goes to the distro; a Windows drive path stays on the host. See [docs/root-fs-routing.md](docs/root-fs-rout

| Mode | What a command can do |
|---|---|
| `read-only` | read the whole distro; a fresh `/dev` is mounted, nothing else is writable |
| `workspace-write` | the above, plus the session workspace; `/tmp` is the distro's real `/tmp` with the session runtime |
| `danger-full-access` | no sandbox |

With `sessionSandbox: false`, a `workspace-write` command gets a private `/tmp` instead of the distro's real one. `read-only` does not mount a writable `/tmp`.

`bubblewrap` is required. If it is missing or broken, confined commands report `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE` and do not run. Setting `sandbox: false` on the owning row disables confinement; the model is told that the operation is unsandboxed.

Enforcement is reported as `partial`. A command inside the distro can still start a Windows executable through `/mnt/c`, and `bubblewrap` cannot control Windows processes. `maskWindowsDrive: true` hides `/mnt` from the confined view unless overridden by `interopVisibility: visible`; this narrows the hole but does not close it. Disabling WSL interop requires a separate distro-level change: set `[interop] enabled=false` in `/etc/wsl.conf`. See [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#sandbox) and [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| every command reports `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE` | install `bubblewrap` in the distro, or set `sandbox: false` |
| the session refuses before the first command | run `pnpm run doctor`; enable systemd and linger, or set `sessionSandbox: false` on `wsl-shell` and `wsl-fs` |
| `glob` and `grep` are slow in the distro | run `pnpm run bootstrap <distro>` and use its printed install command to install `ripgrep` |
| `dsh plugin add` prints nothing | the plugin is already installed; this is success |
| a profile patch for `wsl-shell`/`wsl-fs` changes nothing | those rows are nested inside `preset-wsl`. Run `pnpm run preset --check <patch>`; it fails with the complete block to paste |
| changes under `lib/` have no effect | run `pnpm run sync:windows`, then restart the app |
More error codes and refusals are in [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#error-codes). Everything the plugin does not do is in [docs/LIMITATIONS.md](docs/LIMITATIONS.md).

```bash
pnpm install           # development dependencies
pnpm run build         # compile src/ into lib/ (lib/ is committed)
pnpm test              # style, syntax, build consistency, types, unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage # unit tests with coverage thresholds

The toolchain follows the harness host: Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`. `src/` is TypeScript; `lib/` is generated and must stay in sync. The app loads a Windows-side copy of `lib/`, so run `sync:windows` and restart the app after a build.
